Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:1.hebrew: ואחזוק ולא אחזוק בדלא כתיבא תנאי היא - מצוה שאינה כתובה בפירוש בתורה וראינו שהחזיקו בה, אי אמרינן כיון דאחזוק לדידהו אחזוק נמי לדידן לסמוך עלייהו כי עבדי לצורך עצמן, או אי אמרינן אע"ג דאחזוק לדידהו לא אחזוק לדידן, כלומר לא חשבינן ליה חזקה למסמך עלייהו, תנאי פליגי בה. אחזוק ולא אחזוק, כלומר חזקה או אינה חזקה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:1.english: "Established practice or no established practice" in the case of something not written [in the Torah] is a Tannaitic dispute - A commandment that is not written explicitly in the Torah, and we have seen that they [the Samaritans] maintained it as an established practice - [the question is] whether we say that since it is an established practice for them, it is also an established practice for us, so that we may rely on them when they act for their own needs; or whether we say that even though it is an established practice for them, it is not an established practice for us - meaning, we do not consider it a sufficient established practice to rely on them - this is a matter of Tannaitic dispute. "Established practice or no established practice" means: is it a valid established practice or not.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:2.hebrew: מותר - לאוכלה, ולא חיישינן לחמץ בפסח:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:2.english: It is permitted - to eat it, and we are not concerned about [it containing] chametz on Passover.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:3.hebrew: ואדם יוצא ידי חובתו - שהכתוב קבעו חובה לאכול מצה בלילה ראשונה, דכתיב (שמות י״ב:י״ח) בערב תאכלו מצות, ואם ישב ולא אכל עבר בעשה. ולקמן פריך: כיון דתנא מותר, פשיטא דיוצא בה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:3.english: And a person fulfills his obligation with it - For Scripture established it as an obligation to eat matzah on the first night, as it is written (Exodus 12:18): "In the evening you shall eat unleavened bread," and if one sat and did not eat, he transgressed a positive commandment. And further on [the Gemara] asks: since it was taught that it is permitted, isn't it obvious that one fulfills his obligation with it?

Rashi on Chullin 4a:1:1.english: A string [dekurya] - Strings of slaughtered birds. Reisht, in Old French.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:1.hebrew: אביי - דאמר לעיל: יוצא ונכנס לכתחלה לא שרינן גבי שחיטה, דייק מרישא:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:1.english: Abaye - [This refers to] what he said above: we do not permit, ab initio, [relying on] intermittently going out and coming in with regard to slaughter [as sufficient supervision]. He derives this precisely from the first clause [of the mishna].

Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:2.hebrew: ורבא - דשרי, דייק מסיפא דלא מצריך תנא בדיקה אלא היכא דבא ומצאו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:2.english: And Rava - who permits [in the case where the Jew exits and enters], infers from the latter clause that the Tanna requires examination [i.e., feeding the Samaritan a piece of the slaughtered animal] only in a case where he came and found that he had [already] slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:4:1.hebrew: כעומד על גביו דמי - ועומד על גביו דקתני תנא, היינו יוצא ונכנס:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:4:1.english: It is considered like standing over it - [The phrase] "standing over it," which the tanna teaches, that is [equivalent to a case of] one who exits and enters.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:5:1.hebrew: האי הוא דהוי שחיט שפיר - אותו עוף לבדו שחוט יפה, וזה היה מכירו ואכלו, ואנן היכי נסמוך לאכול האחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:5:1.english: Perhaps it is this one that was properly slaughtered - [Perhaps] only that bird was properly slaughtered, and this [Samaritan] recognized it and ate it, but how can we rely [on that] to eat the rest?

Rashi on Chullin 4a:6:1.hebrew: במכניסן תחת כנפיו - ישראל זה הבודקו, מכניס כל הצפרים תחת כנפי כסותו, ואין הכותי מכיר איזה נתן לו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:6:1.english: By bringing them in under his wings [i.e., garment] - This Israelite who examines him [the Samaritan] brings all the birds in under the wings of his garment, so that the Samaritan (Kuthite) cannot tell which one was given to him.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:7:1.english: He crushed [it] - He squeezed it and pounded it.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:8:1.hebrew: אין שחיטה לעוף מן התורה - משום דלא כתיב זביחה בהדיא אלא בבקר וצאן, דכתיב וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך, ואנן ילפינן בהקישא לקמן (חולין דף כז:) מזאת תורת הבהמה והעוף:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:8:1.english: There is no [Biblically mandated] slaughter for a bird - because [the term] "slaughter" is not written explicitly except regarding cattle and flock, as it is written, "and you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock," and we derive it below (Chullin 27b) by way of an analogy from "this is the law of the animal and the bird."

Rashi on Chullin 4a:9:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך - הך זביחה דכתיב בבקר ובצאן, מי מפרשן הלכותיה בתורה? ואפ"ה סמכי עלייהו, משום דאחזיק להו דאחזיקו בה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:9:1.english: And according to your reasoning - This [very act of] slaughter, which is written [as done] on cattle and on flock - are its halachot spelled out in the Torah? Yet even so we rely upon them, because it has become an established practice, in that they have held fast to it.

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:11:1.hebrew: מצת כותי מותרת - וא"ת: והלא גזרו על פתן, לפי שהיו מבטלין בנין בית המקדש בימי עזרא, כדאמר בפירקין דר"א (פ' לח)? וליכא למימר דהיינו בכותים ראשונים, דכתיב בהם "ואת אלהיהם היו עובדים", דהא קאמר התם: מכאן אמר ר"א, כל האוכל פת כותי כאילו אוכל בשר חזיר. ותנינא נמי לקמן (חולין דף יג.): שחיטת צדוקי לעבודת כוכבים, פתו פת כותי. ואומר ר"ת דמיירי הכא בעיסה דישראל שעשה הכותי ממנה מצה. וא"ת: והיאך יוצא בה, ושמא הוא לא שמר לשם מצה, דהא חשידי אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול? וי"ל כגון שלא אכל הכותי מצה אחרת כל הלילה:
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:11:1.english: The matzah of a Samaritan (Kuthi) is permitted - And if you say: but did they not decree against their bread, because they used to hinder the building of the Beit HaMikdash in the days of Ezra, as is stated in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 38)? And one cannot say that this [decree] refers to the original Samaritans (Kuthim Rishonim), about whom it is written, "and they would worship their gods" - for it states there: from this [incident], Rabbi Eliezer said, anyone who eats the bread of a Samaritan is as if he ate pig meat. And we have also learned further on (Chullin 13a): the slaughter of a Sadducee (Tzeduki) is [treated] as if for idol worship, [and] his bread is [treated] as the bread of a Samaritan. And Rabbeinu Tam says that here we are dealing with dough belonging to a Jew, from which a Samaritan made matzah. And if you say: but how does one fulfill his obligation with it - perhaps he did not guard it for the sake of matzah, since they [Samaritans] are suspect of [transgressing] "you shall not place a stumbling block before the blind"? We can answer: [this works in] a case where the Samaritan ate no other matzah the entire night.

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:1:1.hebrew: דקוריא - סל, כמו דקוריא דפרק השוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פד.), ודמפנין (שבת קכז.):
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:1:1.english: Dekurya - A basket, like [the word] "dekurya" [used] in the chapter "HaSocher Et HaPoalim" (Bava Metzia 84a), and in [the chapter dealing with] "clearing out" (Shabbat 127a).

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:6:1.hebrew: מכניס איזמל בזכרים - סימני שמעתתא דרב מנשה, דהא מכילתא הן: הך ד"מכניס תחת כנפיו", ולקמן בפרק שני (חולין דף לא.) "איזמל שאין לו קרנים", ובפרק אלו טרפות (לקמן חולין דף נא.) "הנהו דיכרי דגנבי גנבי, אין חוששין לריסוק אברים". מיהו גם במקומות אחרים יש, כדאשכחנא בפרק ב' דיבמות (דף כה.) דאמר רב מנשה: גזלן דדבריהם כשר לעדות אשה, ובפרק מי שהחשיך (שבת קנו.) אמר רב מנשה: חדא קמי חדא, תרי קמי תרי, שפיר דמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:6:1.english: Inserts a knife, among males - These are the mnemonic markers (simanim) for the teachings (shema'ata) of Rav Menashe, for these are indeed separate teachings: this one, of "inserting [the hand] under its wings" [in our sugya]; and further on, in the second chapter (Chullin 31a), "a slaughtering knife that has no protruding points (keranim)"; and in the chapter "Eilu Treifot" (below, Chullin 51a), "those rams that thieves stole - we do not suspect that their limbs were crushed." However, there are also [teachings of Rav Menashe] in other places, as we find in the second chapter of Yevamot (25a), where Rav Menashe says: a robber [disqualified] only by rabbinic law is valid to testify on behalf of a woman [regarding her husband's death, to permit her to remarry]. And in the chapter "Mi SheHechshich" (Shabbat 156a), Rav Menashe said: one facing one, two facing two, is fine.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:12:1.hebrew: שאין בקיאין - אין יודעין לשומרה ולהבחין בין שיאור לסידוק, בין הכסיפו פניו ללא הכסיפו פניו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:12:1.english: For they are not expert - They do not know how to watch over it [the dough, to keep it from leavening], nor to distinguish between [the stage called] "se'or" and [the stage called] "sidduk" [cracking] - that is, between [dough] whose surface has turned pale and [dough] whose surface has not turned pale.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:14:1.english: Obviously - that one fulfills his obligation with it, since it is permitted.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:14:2.english: Lest you say - Even though it is obvious to us that they did not let it become leavened, and it is permitted to eat, nevertheless, they are not expert in this - that one must perform "guarding" for the sake of the matzah of the mitzvah - and since guarding was not performed on it, we do not fulfill our obligation with it at all; just as is the case with the flour and dough of idolaters that come before us before the idolater has baked them, and we see that they have not leavened - for we hold that they are permitted to eat - yet we do not fulfill our obligation with them, as we learned: "The flour and dough of idolaters - a person may fill his stomach with them, provided that he eats an olive's-bulk of matzah last."

Rashi on Chullin 4a:14:3.english: And Rabbi Eliezer forbids [it] - Even to eat it.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:14:4.english: He holds: [Samaritans] are not expert in guarding [the matzah from becoming leavened] - We do not have this reading. And the reason [for Rabbi Eliezer's ruling] is because of concern for leavening. And according to the one who does have this reading, he explains it: they are not expert in guarding it from becoming leavened. And some explain that Rabbi Eliezer prohibits [using it] to fulfill one's obligation with it on Passover, but this is not correct, since that is not the language of a prohibition.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:15:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו - מילתא דכתיבא באורייתא, ולא ידעינן בהו דאחזיקו בה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:15:1.english: There is [a difference] between them - A matter that is written in the Torah, but we do not know about them that they have adopted it.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:15:2.hebrew: ת"ק - דלא איירי בחזקה כלל, אכתיבא דאורייתא קפיד, ותנא מצה, וה"ה לכל הכתובים בתורה, אע"ג דלא ידעינן אי אחזיקו בה אי לא, אחזוק סמכינן עלייהו, דכיון דכתיבא ודאי אחזוק בה. ור"א אוסר אפילו אחזיקו בה, דהא אינם בקיאין בדקדוקי מצות. ורשב"ג אתא למימר אחזוק אין, לא אחזוק לא. ולאו היינו תנאי דאמר לעיל, עד מסקנא דמילתא:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:15:2.english: Tanna Kamma - [This means] that he is not speaking of an established practice (chazakah) at all; rather, he is particular about what is written in the Torah, and he teaches [the case of] matzah, and the same applies to everything written in the Torah. Even though we do not know whether they [the Samaritans] have adopted it as an established practice or not, we rely on [assuming] an established practice regarding them, since, once it is written [in the Torah], they certainly have adopted it as an established practice. And Rabbi Eliezer forbids it even if they have adopted it as an established practice, because they are not expert in the fine details of the commandments. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say: if they adopted it as an established practice - yes [it is permitted]; if they did not adopt it as an established practice - no [it is not]. And this is not the same as the tannaitic dispute mentioned above - [that will emerge only] at the conclusion of the matter.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:16:1.hebrew: כל מצוה - משמע דלרבויי אתא, אפילו הנך דלא איירי בהו. וכיון דאוקמן דאהני דאיירי בהו לעיל קאי, דהיינו בדכתיבי, למעוטי אתא:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:16:1.english: Any mitzva - [The word "any"] implies that it comes to include, even those [mitzvot] that were not discussed [previously]. But since we have established that this [statement] refers to those that were discussed above, i.e., those that are written [in the Torah], it [actually] comes to exclude [anything beyond those].

Rashi on Chullin 4a:16:2.hebrew: אם החזיקו מיבעי ליה - דהשתא הוי משמע שפיר דפליג אתרוייהו, לת"ק דשרי בלא חזקה, ולר"א דאוסר אפילו החזיקו, ואתא איהו למימר: אם החזיקו מדקדקין בה ומותר, ודלא כר"א, הא לא אחזיקו אסור, ודלא כת"ק דשרי בלא אחזיקו. אבל השתא דקתני כל, משמע דאפילו הנך דלא כתיבין נמי קאמר, דסמכינן אחזקייהו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:16:2.english: He should have said, "if they were accustomed" - Because now it would properly imply that he disagrees with both of them: with the first (anonymous) tanna, who permits it without their being accustomed [to it], and with Rabbi Eliezer, who forbids it even if they were accustomed. And he [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] comes to say: if they were accustomed, they are scrupulous about it and it is permitted - and this is unlike Rabbi Eliezer; but if they were not accustomed, it is forbidden - and this is unlike the first tanna, who permits it even without their being accustomed. But now that he teaches "any [commandment]," it implies that he means even those [commandments] that are not written [explicitly in the Torah] - that we rely on their being accustomed to it.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:17:1.hebrew: אלא איכא בינייהו דלא כתיבא ואחזוק בה, ת"ק סבר - מצה וכל דדמיא ליה דכתיבא, סמכינן עלייהו בין אחזוק בין לא אחזוק, ודלא כתיבא לא סמכינן עלייהו ואפילו אחזוק. ור"א סבר, אפילו כתיבא ואחזוק לא סמכינן עלייהו. ורשב"ג סבר, כל מצוה שהחזיקו, ואע"ג דלא כתיבא סמכינן עלייהו, כיון דאחזוק אחזוק. והיינו תנאי דלעיל, ת"ק ורשב"ג:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:17:1.english: Rather, [the practical difference] between them is [a mitzva] that is not written and that they embraced; the first tanna holds - [that with regard to] matzah and anything similar to it that is written, we rely on them whether they embraced [its observance] or did not embrace it, but [with regard to] something not written, we do not rely on them even if they embraced it. And Rabbi Eliezer holds: even [if it is] written and they embraced it, we do not rely on them. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds: any mitzva that they embraced, even though it is not written, we rely on them, since once they embraced it, it is [firmly] embraced. And this is the same as the dispute of the tanna'im cited above, the first tanna and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:19:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא התירא ואיסורא - קמיה, שבידו להכשירה ובידו לנבלה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:19:1.english: Since there is a permitted and a prohibited [manner of slaughter] - before him, since it is in his power to render it fit [for consumption], and it is in his power to render it a neveilah (an improperly slaughtered carcass).

Rashi on Chullin 4a:20:1.english: He does not go to the trouble - If he does not find it [the knife] to be good, he will not go and seek out another knife.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:21:1.hebrew: תניא דמסייע לך - דכל מי שאינו עושה להכעיס, ואיכא התירא קמיה, לא שביק התירא ואכיל איסורא:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:21:1.english: It is taught in a baraita that supports you - For anyone who does not act out of spite, and there is a permitted [food] before him, does not leave the permitted [food] and eat the forbidden [food].

Rashi on Chullin 4a:21:2.hebrew: של עוברי עבירה - שאין מבערין חמץ בפסח מפני הפסידה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:21:2.english: Of transgressors - For they do not remove [their] chametz on Passover, because of the loss [it would cause them].

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:17:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דלא כתיבא ואחזיקו בה כו' - בפ"ק דגיטין (דף י.) מוכח דכתיבא ולא אחזיקו בה נמי איכא בינייהו, דלת"ק מהני, ולרשב"ג לא מהני. והכא לא נקט אלא לא כתיבא ואחזיקו בה, משום דאשחיטת כותי בעי לאתויי תנאי. א"נ דלא אתא לשנויי אלא מה שהקשה, אם החזיקו בה מבעי ליה. ושם פירשנו:
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:17:1.english: There is a difference between them [regarding a case] that is not written but that they embraced, etc. - In the first chapter of Gittin (10a) it is proven that [a case] that is written but that they did not embrace is also a difference between them: for the first tanna it is effective [i.e., one may rely on the Samaritans], while for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel it is not effective. And here [the Gemara] mentioned only [the case of] "not written but they embraced it," because with regard to the slaughter of a Samaritan (Kuti) it needed to bring in the [earlier] Tannaitic dispute [cited above, regarding the matza of a Samaritan]. Alternatively, [the Gemara] did not come to resolve anything other than the difficulty it had raised - that it should have said "if they embraced it" - and there [in Gittin] we have explained this.
